claims.text: Conventional pressureless sintering of single-phase ZrB2 requires temperatures above 2300 °C.
Conventionally pressureless-sintered single-phase ZrB2 has a relatively porous microstructure.
Conventionally prepared single-phase ZrB2 has limited mechanical integrity.
SPS can densify single-phase ZrB2 at approximately 1900–2100 °C.
SPS produces a denser and more uniform ZrB2 microstructure with lower residual porosity than conventional pressureless sintering.
Rapid localized Joule heating during SPS accelerates ZrB2 densification.
Electric-field-assisted mass transport during SPS contributes to lower-temperature densification of ZrB2.
Applied pressure and high heating rates during SPS create a compact grain-boundary structure with fewer residual pores.
Lower residual porosity reduces penetration of the liquid plating bath into ZrB2.
Reduced liquid penetration suppresses detrimental hole formation during plating-bath service.
Suppressing porosity, liquid penetration, and hole formation improves long-term structural integrity during plating-bath exposure.
SPS will reduce the required ZrB2 processing temperature by approximately 200–300 °C relative to conventional pressureless sintering.
SPS-prepared ZrB2 will have lower porosity than conventionally sintered ZrB2.
SPS-prepared ZrB2 will resist hole formation better during prolonged liquid plating-bath exposure than conventionally sintered ZrB2.
SPS-prepared ZrB2 will undergo less mechanical degradation during prolonged liquid plating-bath exposure than conventionally sintered ZrB2.
The relevant liquid plating-bath operating conditions promote liquid infiltration and pore formation in conventionally prepared ZrB2.
Conventionally pressureless-sintered ZrB2 exhibits more pronounced degradation under liquid plating conditions than SPS-prepared ZrB2.
